data_limitations: KO reports net operating revenues on us-gaap:Revenues. The core registry retired that element as a source of the `revenue` metric in decision 2.99, because the element's own definition is broader than the metric, so no production revenue role exists for KO on the element KO files. The registry's accepted revenue element, us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, is not filed by KO at all. The lane reads the element KO files and names what it reads.

The registry declares no `marketable_securities_current` metric, so it has no standing to rule on this component and the filed-bridge specification governs it. KO's 'Marketable securities' line is carried on us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesCurrent through 2020-12-31 and on us-gaap:MarketableSecurities afterwards; the two carry the same filed value on the dates at which both are reported, so the change is a re-tagging of the same quantity and is disclosed as a basis break. KO's separate 'Short-term investments' line is not part of this component.

The registry declares no `commercial_paper` metric, so it has no standing to rule on this component. KO does not carry a commercial paper line on the face of its balance sheet: KO's balance sheet carries 'Loans and notes payable' as the total of its short-term borrowings, and KO discloses commercial paper as a component of that line in its debt note. KO files this element annually only until 2023, so a bridge that holds it is incomplete at most quarterly dates.

us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent is registry-qualified for KO and is filed through 2024-03-29. From 2023-12-31 KO carries the same line on us-gaap:LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations, whose definition includes the lease obligation where the earlier element excluded it, so the element change is also a scope change and is disclosed as a basis break.

us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent is registry-qualified for KO and is filed through 2024-03-29. Its successor carries the current maturities of long-term debt from 2023-12-31 and, like its noncurrent counterpart, includes the lease obligation.

Cover-page shares outstanding, taken as filed and never adjusted for a split, paired with the as-traded close. The registry declares no metric for it; the production rule for pairing it with the as-traded close governs the role.

The capture's acceptance index covers the issuer's periodic filings only, so a fact first published in another form becomes knowable in this lane at the next periodic filing that carries it. The lane therefore never uses a value before it was public, and it may use a value later than it first became public.
